evals.prompt: Our support team keeps asking an agent to turn incident notes into a customer-safe postmortem. I have three real incident reports, two examples the team approved, and reviewer comments rejecting leaked internal hostnames. Create a portable skill package that captures this workflow. It must work offline in both Codex and Claude Code.
evals.expected_output: A small new skill grounded in the supplied artifacts, with explicit triggers, inputs, outputs, privacy gotchas, portable frontmatter, proportionate evals, and validation evidence.
assertions: The response first evaluates whether a skill is the correct primitive
The response asks for or inspects the named incident reports, approved examples, and rejection evidence before drafting generic guidance
The resulting design explicitly answers who invokes, what fires on invariants, and the token budget
The proposed frontmatter is portable and the description includes capability, triggers, and exclusions without summarizing the workflow

evals.prompt: Make me a skill that guarantees every commit message starts with one of feat:, fix:, docs:, or chore:. This is only for this repository, and our CI can run a shell command on every commit. I don't have examples because the rule is exactly that regex.
evals.expected_output: A recommendation to use a deterministic repository mechanism such as a commit-msg hook or CI validator, with at most a small advisory instruction if useful, rather than manufacturing a skill.
assertions: The response does not assume a skill is the right primitive
The invariant is assigned to a real hook or validator mechanism rather than advisory prose
The response explains why a project-local deterministic rule does not justify a standalone skill

evals.prompt: We already have skills/release-notes/SKILL.md. Please improve it, run the old and new versions against ten prompts, and tell me which is better.
evals.expected_output: A clear boundary statement that creation does not cover updating or comparative benchmarking, with future handoffs named and only a narrow fallback offered if explicitly requested.
assertions: The response identifies the existing-skill request as a future handoff to toolboxmd-updating-skills
The response identifies the better-version comparison as a future handoff to toolboxmd-benchmarking-skills
The response does not construct an updater or a creator-versus-creator benchmark workflow
